fields.question: Why isn't trajectory learnability just success reward?
fields.answer: Success describes outcome, whereas current student mastery determines learning value. Token likelihood changes between successful reference and current policy reweight offline traces for remaining opportunity.
fields.example: Two correct solutions can differ because student already knows one and misses the other's key step.

fields.question: How does offline reweighting differ from collecting fresh on-policy data?
fields.answer: Weight allocates budget inside existing coverage. New sampling reaches new states. OPD in the name doesn't make replay current-policy generation.
fields.example: Reweighting a cache cannot create an absent solution.

fields.question: Does local learnability aggregation include full GPU training?
fields.answer: No. It implements token aggregation and trajectory weighting. Score identical text/prefix under both versions and record them; don't subtract different responses.
fields.example: Old model scoring A and current model scoring B confounds text change.

fields.question: Why compare token likelihoods rather than rank offline traces by reward?
fields.answer: Success alone doesn't locate learning opportunities. Train reference on successes and compare likelihoods to current policy to estimate learnability. Depends on reference and offline coverage; local kernel only.
fields.example: Reweight two correct traces differently when one is mastered and the other has a difficult turning point.

fields.question: Why grow draft heads during RL in GrowMTP?
fields.answer: Main policy evolves, making static drafters stale. Train multi-token heads with rollout acceptance to follow policy. Faster drafting isn't task capability improvement.
fields.example: If policy learns new phrasing, drafter should propose it to retain acceptance.

fields.question: How does acceptance-depth learning differ from equal future-head supervision?
fields.answer: A later head helps only after earlier proposals are accepted. Depth coupling reflects use, unlike equal head contributions. Still verify with target.
fields.example: Head three saves a step only if the first two proposals pass.

fields.question: Why decouple GrowMTP gradients, and was speed measured?
fields.answer: Keep draft optimization from inadvertently changing main RL objective. Local code tests acceptance-depth loss only, without measured GPU throughput. End-to-end speed needs timing.
fields.example: More accurate drafting may also add compute.

fields.question: Why train by actual accepted depth and detach from backbone gradients?
fields.answer: Later drafts only contribute after earlier acceptance, so observed depth reflects use. Decoupling protects reward learning. Hardware and verification costs determine actual speed; local loss isn't acceleration or capability evidence.
fields.example: A third draft token isn't as reachable as first, and improving it doesn't prove stronger policy.

fields.question: Why restart STRIDE-OPD from the weakest correct turn?
fields.answer: A cached learnable state focuses budget on barely mastered turns rather than regenerating familiar prefix. Correct qualification ensures a valid starting point.
fields.example: Retry from a second turn that only just succeeds once the first is stable.

fields.question: How does early stopping differ from uniform truncation?
fields.answer: Teacher cumulative confidence triggers a state-dependent stop paired with prefix restart. A fixed length limit changes coverage differently; shortness doesn't guarantee completion or savings.
fields.example: A solved trace and exploratory trace need not stop at the same token count.

fields.question: Can STRIDE restore any environment from cached prefix text?
fields.answer: Align cached prefix with executed actions and observations. Text alone may omit environment state. Local state machine isn't LLM rollout throughput.
fields.example: Do not duplicate a tool side effect on restore and call it the same state.

fields.question: Why pair early stopping and restart from weakest correct turn?
fields.answer: Teacher cumulative confidence avoids spending on low-value continuations. A weak but correct cached turn reassigns budget to practice. These are distinct choices, not jumps to gold. No real-model throughput validation.
fields.example: Stop an uninformative continuation, then retry from an earlier barely successful turn rather than repeatedly replay the familiar beginning.

fields.question: What dependency does data-free OPD reduce?
fields.answer: Teacher-generated prompts reduce collection of a separate post-training problem bank. Teacher knowledge and sampling still provide information.
fields.example: Teacher can create exercises without a human bank using existing learned skills.

fields.question: How does generated curriculum trade off with fixed public tasks?
fields.answer: Generated tasks can target teacher skills but repeat or omit topics. Fixed banks have auditable coverage and collection cost. Validate quality; linguistic format isn't task validity.
fields.example: A teacher repeating linear equations does not cover geometry automatically.

fields.question: Has local DF-OPD generated a real natural-language training set?
fields.answer: No. Only policy-feature diagnostics for generated questions. Need actual generation, filtering and distillation provenance, not changing candidate indices.
fields.example: A feature ID isn't a verified math problem.

fields.question: Why isn't self-generated data-free OPD independent of prior knowledge?
fields.answer: Teacher parameters, sampling and filters determine curriculum even without a separate task bank. Generated tasks can be repetitive/unreliable. Local diagnostics have not generated a natural-language dataset.
fields.example: Generating code exercises avoids human curation but repeated loop problems do not teach omitted concurrency.

fields.question: Why constrain LOCUS updates to task-related low rank?
fields.answer: Compact directions can improve token efficiency while limiting unrelated drift. If subspace misses key skills, performance can suffer.
fields.example: Removing redundant language may not require unrestricted changes to all parameters.

fields.question: How does low-rank learning differ from truncating output?
fields.answer: Train more concise behavior rather than deleting already generated steps. Check correctness alongside length, not shorter alone.
fields.example: Omitting repetition and cutting a proof's conclusion both shorten text but differ in quality.

fields.question: Does local LOCUS SVD train a real language model?
fields.answer: No. It projects policy gradients in a feature subspace. Check rank, orthogonality and gradient paths. A random low-rank matrix isn't learned semantic direction.
fields.example: Projection success doesn't establish coverage of core reasoning.

fields.question: Why can task-related low-rank updates shorten responses without truncation?
fields.answer: Learning operates on parameter directions and aims to preserve task-relevant changes. Truncation deletes content afterward, potentially essential. Validate subspace, correctness and efficiency; proxy SVD isn't LLM evidence.
fields.example: Learn to omit redundant checks, not cut the second half of every proof.

fields.question: Why combine multiple signals for adaptive OPD gating?
fields.answer: Entropy, uncertainty, reference drift and teacher/student gap capture different conditions. Combine them to allocate per-token forward/reverse KL; signal utility must be validated.
fields.example: Teacher confident but far from reference differs from uncertain but close to student.

fields.question: How does per-token FKL/RKL differ from one ratio per reply?
fields.answer: Token gates vary coverage vs concentration by position; fixed mixture applies everywhere. Flexibility increases tuning/overfit risk; diagnostics aren't consistent wins.
fields.example: A reasoning branch and predictable format token need not receive the same mix.

fields.question: Can local four-signal gates qualify for capability promotion?
fields.answer: No. Deterministic mechanism tests don't establish full-model effects or fair compute. Specify direction, signal versions and gradients; registry changes are not training.
fields.example: One improved small-candidate score doesn't generalize to open language.

fields.question: Why mix FKL and RKL per token rather than select one direction per answer?
fields.answer: Uncertainty, gaps and reference drift vary by token. Allocate coverage and concentration accordingly. Gate is a supervision heuristic, not truth, and local tests don't show stable superiority.
fields.example: Preserve multiple options at a pivotal branch and use concentrated guidance for settled format.
